baseline.project_title: Citation-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Traceable Academic Literature Synthesis
baseline.rationale: Students and researchers using large language models for literature reviews frequently encounter fabricated citations, unverified claims, and weak alignment to stated research gaps. Combining retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with verifiable source grounding and structured rubric evaluation can improve provenance and source-selection reliability.
research_gaps: Large language models lack reliable source provenance and frequently hallucinate unsupported claims or citations during academic literature synthesis.
Automated literature evaluation pipelines often lack transparent, multi-criterion rubric scoring and quote-level verification back to source pages.
Existing RAG benchmarks rarely evaluate end-to-end citation faithfulness, gap alignment, and human-in-the-loop validation for scholarly synthesis.
